title: TRUCKER FOUND DEAD
full_story:
The Effingham County Coroner’s Office reports that a Texas trucker was found dead in Effingham Monday afternoon.

The trucker has been identified as 50-year-old John Savelli of Humble, Texas.

The Effingham City Police Department notified the Coroner’s Office at about 2 pm Monday of a death.  Deputy Coroner Lauren Heuerman and County Coroner Kim Rhodes arrived at the truck stop and were advised that the trucking company from Texas was attempting to locate their driver, who was parked at that location.

Effingham City Police located the vehicle and discovered the dead man in the cab of the semi.  There were no visible injuries or trauma.  The Coroner’s Office transported Savelli to the Effingham County Morgue, then notified next-of-kin in Texas.

Toxicology samples were taken and medical records were requested from the primary physician in Texas. Toxicology results should be available in two to three weeks.  A preliminary investigation indicated that Savelli’s death was natural.

The Effingham City Police Department and the Effingham County Coroner’s Office are continuing their investigation.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross has an urgent need for blood donors of all blood types.  Blood donors are urgently needed because there has been a troubling drop in appointments which is putting pressure on the national blood supply.

There is a Blood Drive today, from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  Donors at this drive will receive a $15 gift card by email.  There are 2 Power Red appointments left at this drive and 7 regular blood drive appointments available.  Walk ins will be welcome.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).

The next American Red Cross Blood Drive in Flora will be on July 10th at the Clay County Health Department from 1 to 5 pm.

title: COUNTERFEIT BILLS
full_story:
Local and area law enforcement authorities are alerting the public after reports of counterfeit $100 bills circulating in the area.

According to law enforcement the fake bills may appear legitimate at first glance but are marked “For Motion Picture Use,” indicating they are not legal tender.

Customers and businesses are urged to carefully inspect $100 bills before accepting them and to watch specifically for the printed phrase “For Motion Picture Use.”

Anyone who encounters suspicious currency should report it immediately and exercise extra caution during cash transactions.

title: OCC MASSAGE THERAPY SIGN UP
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting new students for Fall 2026.

Designed with busy adults in mind, the program offers convenient evening classes that allow students to pursue a rewarding new career without putting life on hold.  Best of all, the certificate can be completed in just one year.

While enrolled, students gain the skills needed to work in the wellness field of massage therapy, mastering professional massage techniques through hands-on classroom instruction and clinical experience. The program’s clinical opportunities, which are open to the public, provide students with valuable practice working with a variety of clients in a real-world setting.

Olney Central College is recognized as a National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage & Bodywork (NCBTMB) Assigned School.  This designation confirms that OCC’s Massage Therapy Program meets the high standards of excellence established by the NCBTMB.  It also ensures that after successfully completing state licensure requirements, graduates are eligible to pursue NCBTMB board certification; the highest credential available in the massage therapy profession.

Enrollment is limited.  To reserve a spot, apply by July 15th at www.iecc.edu/apply.

title: GRAND LEVEE JUNE 20th
full_story:
The Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site will host the annual Grand Levee, a celebration of the grand receptions held during the 1800s to honor government dignitaries and important visitors, on Saturday, June 20th.

The event, featuring an entire day of activities and entertainment, is free and open to the public.  The historic site is at 315 West Gallatin Street in Vandalia.

Festivities will begin at 10 am on the lawn of the Vandalia Statehouse with period arts and crafts demonstrations, children’s activities, painting and woodcarving by the Fayette County Art Connection, and performances by the Dulcimer Guy.  Food and beverages will be available for purchase, and the Rotary Club will provide free funnel cakes.

Other activities include performances by the Clockwork Clown, Times in History: A Traveling Museum, Professor Farquar and Polecat Annie, and the Singing Blacksmith Bryan Dale Headley.  Families can enjoy giant bubble activities with Wild Foam Adventures and get up close with animals with the Lucky R Mobile Petting Zoo.

For a schedule of events and more information, visit the Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site on Facebook or call 618-283-1161.

The Vandalia Statehouse is the oldest surviving capitol building in Illinois.  It served as the state capital from 1836 to 1839 and is open to the public between 9 am and 5 pm Wednesday through Sunday.

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, September 25th, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 a. from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: LAWS TAKING EFFECT JULY 1ST
full_story:
While Illinois families won’t see gas prices increase July 1st, they will see a record $55.9 billion budget with over $800 million in tax increases and new laws take effect.

Referred to as Deb’s Law, patients with a terminal disease may ask a doctor to prescribe aid-in-dying medication allowing them to end their life “in a peaceful manner.”  Senate Bill 1950 was originally titled “Sanitary Food Preparation” and amended in the last week of the 2025 regular session to the “End-of-Life Options for Terminally Ill Patients Act.”

House Bill 3851 adds to the bullying prevention section of the school code.  “Posting or distributing sexually explicit images” is considered a form of bullying.  Beginning in the 2026-2027 school year, “‘cyber-bullying’ also includes the posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means” if the post creates fear or harm for the student, hurts the student’s physical or mental health, or interferes with the student’s academic performance or the ability to participate in other services, activities or privileges provided by the school.

A school bus driver has a new permit option.  House Bill 2962 creates a specialized school bus driver permit to operate smaller passenger vehicles and a “multifunction school activity bus” designed to carry up to 15 passengers when being used for curriculum-related activities such as transportation between home and school, to a vocational school or for a field trip.  The bill gives districts more flexibility for curriculum-related transportation while maintaining strict safety standards.

House Bill 1226 raises the age for in-person license renewal to 79, up from 75.  The bill also adds to the Illinois Vehicle Code that an applicant over age 87, or 75 if the person holds a commercial driver’s license, “must prove, by actual demonstration,” that they can safely operate a vehicle.

Passed in 2024 during the 103rd Illinois General Assembly, Senate Bill 1 streamlines bureaucracy and accomplishes a recommendation from the bipartisan Illinois Commission on Equitable Early Childhood Education and Care Funding.  Two years after Pritzker signed it into law, the new Department of Early Childhood launches July 1st, overseeing programs and services that have been handled by three state agencies.

title: SUBARU RECALL
full_story:
Subaru is recalling nearly 70,000 vehicles for a defect that could cause the moonroof glass panels to detach.  The recall includes nearly 70,000 2026 Subaru Forester and Forester Hybrid vehicles.

The impacted Subaru Foresters were produced from June 19, 2025, to March 13, 2026.  The affected hybrid models were produced between February 20th and March 17th.

The vehicles may have been manufactured without the power moonroof being properly installed due to a lack of primer, according to the recall notice.  Over time, the bond between the sliding frame and the glass can deteriorate, causing the moonroof glass to become detached while the car is operating.

The automaker said a detached glass panel could raise the risk of a crash or injury for other drivers.

title: TOP STATE & LOCAL TAXES
full_story:
Illinois had the 10th-highest state and local tax collections per person in fiscal 2023, according to a tax policy nonprofit.

State residents paid an average of $8,339 per capita that year, $1,301 over the national average, data from the Tax Foundation show.

High taxes weigh heavily on households and business competitiveness. Just over 58% of Illinois voters rank taxes as one of the state’s top two issues.

Illinois is losing more residents to other places in the country than virtually any other state, ranking third-worst in the country in losses from domestic migration.  In the year ending July 1, 2025, more than 40,000 residents moved to other states, with eight of 11 metro areas and more than half the counties in Illinois seeing net outmigration.

Not just residents leave.  From 1994 to 2023, Illinois lost over 2,600 businesses, according to federal data, with the highest numbers in the most recent of those years.

Many industries have shown exceptional growth in Illinois.  One is construction, which has created 4,000 to 8,000 jobs in the state, in large part because of the boom in AI data centers.

Illinois faces among the highest tax burdens in the nation, businesses leaving, high unemployment and low social mobility.  The state should focus on long-term reform that reins in spending and creates an environment in which businesses can thrive.  That is the path to a stronger economy in Illinois.
